Option B. Cartography, survey, data collection and GIS/GPS are all techniques a geographer uses rather than parts of the subject matter. The chapter groups exactly these under Geographic Techniques in its diagram of the subject, and its list of the skills of a geographer names making maps, land surveying with instruments and advanced technology, and data collection using surveys, photographs and satellite images. It adds that the use of GPS and GIS has become a mandatory aspect of geographical studies.

Each of the other three groups mixes categories. In A, Geomorphology, Climatology and Biogeography are fields of Physical Geography, but Historical Geography is a branch of Human Geography. In C, forest conservation, wildlife conservation and culture conservation are all conservation work, but tourism is not. In D, Political, Population and Economic Geography are all branches of Human Geography, whereas Physical Geography is one of the subject's two major divisions and so does not sit at the same level as the other three.
